correctness.rationale: Every nonalgebraic type is uniquely indexed by a level j and an E_j-class of the finite base. Distinct types have a forced mutual distance equal to their hierarchy merge level; identical types permit every positive distance up to their attachment level. For each prescribed distance s, the matrix has isolated positive singleton blocks for higher types and a complete-multipartite-with-hub block for every E_s cluster. Replacing each child representative by its difference with the hub, and each other descendant by its difference with its child representative, is an explicit unimodular integer basis and yields only +1, -1 and 0. Every field rank, Smith factor and inertia follows. A standalone checker directly reconstructed 638 finite ultrametric bases, compared all 112842 pair-feasibility entries and verified exact integral congruences plus modular ranks; no computational extrapolation is used in the all-size proof.

originality.rationale: The exact mathematical object is an integer matrix on complete nonalgebraic one-point types over any named finite ultrametric base, with a prescribed distance between two distinct realizations. Primary sources give finite ultrametric amalgamation, tree representation, and distance constraints, but not the explicit arbitrary-base integral congruence, Smith form or recovery of threshold partition counts by inertia. Accessible published ultrametric results on colored gaps, k-variable theories and color refinement use different matrices or no pair-feasibility matrices. The check is best-knowledge, not a uniqueness certificate.
residual_risks: An unindexed classical tree-incidence or hierarchical matrix diagonalization might imply an equivalent unit-congruence theorem.
Not every older paper on ultrametric association schemes or nested equivalence relations could be inspected; no claim of exhaustive priority is made.
Some historical literature and informal lecture notes on tree-incidence matrices remain outside the inspected material.

value.rationale: Distance-specific amalgamation compatibility matrices are canonical finite invariants of the named-base type space, not a synthetically chosen submatrix. The result classifies their entire integral arithmetic over every finite ultrametric base, finds that all torsion vanishes despite possible rank collapse, and recovers each old ball-partition count as a negative inertia index. This exact hierarchy-to-logic inversion and all-field rigidity are structural information not supplied by scalar one-type counts, generic tree representation, or ordinary metric examples.
